newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown says EMU criteria must not be fudged.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown says EMU criteria must not be fudged.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown said on Monday that the "convergence criteria" for joining a single European currency must not be fudged.
"I do not believe it's right to fudge criteria once they're established," he said in an interview with BBC radio from Luxembourg, where he was attending a meeting of European Union finance ministers.

Brown said jobs and growth should be the EU's main focus in the months ahead and measures to prepare for the single currency should be accompanied by action to create jobs and increase labour market flexibility.
"It is important to recognise that that is part of the new agenda for Europe," he added.
Asked whether the single currency now looked less likely to happen on schedule in 1999 than it did six months ago, Brown replied: "Nobody can be sure about what's going to happen."
Britain had said it was highly unlikely it would want to join in the first wave but it would make a hard-headed assessment of whether joining was in its best interests, he said.
